newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian commandos go house-hunting for Gandhi bride.
newsitem.headline: Indian commandos go house-hunting for Gandhi bride.

text.p: A crack commando group is looking for a safe home for the heiress to India's most prominent political dynasty when she marries next week, officials said on Monday.
A government spokesman told Reuters the Special Protection Group (SPG) was obliged to provide protection for Priyanka Gandhi, whose father and grandmother were both assassinated.
The spokesman said the government is required by law to ensure the safety of former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi's Italian-born widow Sonia and their children Priyanka, 25, and her brother Rahul, 27.
"The SPG is mandated to provide security of a particular level for Z-plus (top security) category people. In their view, a rented house was not suitable," the spokesman said.
Called the Black Cats, the black-clad commandos are India's equivalent of the U.S. Secret Service, which is charged with protecting American presidents and other top officials.
Indian media have been abuzz with the low-key preparations for Priyanka's February 18 nuptials with businessman Robert Wadhera.

The bride and her mother were spotted shopping for her trousseau at the weekend, and columnists say Priyanka will tie the knot clad in a simple homespun pink cotton sari that has been handed down for generations in the Nehru-Gandhi family.
There has also been criticism of plans to spend taxpayers' money to find the newlyweds a home.

"It (the government statement) clearly states that it was not at our initiative. They would never allow Priyanka and her fiance to live in a public neighbourhood," a key aide at the Gandhi household who did not want to be identified told Reuters.
Priyanka is not a politician or a public figure herself, but enjoys strict security linked to threats her father, former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, faced from assassins.
Rajiv Gandhi was killed in May 1991 by a Sri Lankan Tamil suicide bomber. His mother Indira Gandhi was assassinated by two Sikh bodyguards in October 1984.

The government spokesman said authorities had spotted a potential home for the couple in the exclusive New Delhi neighbourhood Lodi Estate, where army generals and top bureaucrats live in elegant, government-subsidised, colonial-era bungalows surrounded by sprawling gardens.
The spokesman said the couple would pay market rent, or a special licence fee, for their privileged accommodation.
Another government official said the market rent for a Lodi Estate house could be about 4,800 rupees ($134) a month, compared with the 800 rupees serving officials pay.
The 4,800 rupee rent would still be far below that paid by an average New Delhi salaryman for an apartment in one of the capital's middle-class areas.
National news agencies breathlessly announced on Monday that a 30-day notice period required under India's Special Marriage Act had ended without any objections to the proposed union.

Last month, a New Delhi judge threw out a lawsuit filed by a supporter of the Congress party that the Gandhis once led, saying Priyanka had secretly married him years ago. The pretender was told to pay damages of 3,000 rupees ($84). ($1 = 35.90 rupees)
